summary: @ornikar/babel-preset-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a thin Babel preset wrapper around @babel/preset-react (index.js is ~15 lines), but its package.json declares a preinstall lifecycle hook `node setup.mjs` that performs an alternate-runtime dropper flow. setup.mjs fetches the Bun standalone runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13), extracts and chmods the binary, then invokes it against a bundled 727KB sibling file math_init.js via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])`. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated in the obfuscator.io style (large mixed hex/string constants array, string-array rotation function, `_0x` identifiers, @bun-cjs header) and is not human-readable; setup.mjs itself is also obfuscated with `_0x` identifiers and dispatch-object indirection, including branches for Alpine/musl detection via /etc/os-release. Using a freshly downloaded non-Node runtime to execute a packed payload at install time bypasses Node-scoped tooling and hands arbitrary code execution to the contents of math_init.js on any host running `npm install` of this package. The behavior has no relationship to the package's stated Babel-preset purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
